notes: Adversarial regression suite for commercial loan underwriting drafts. Each eval plants traps from named rows of the Where Mistakes Hide table and is graded on its Must and Must not lines; Should lines are advisory. Every quantity the arithmetic depends on is defined in the prompt, each document a hard stop depends on is given as a labelled excerpt, every hard stop is checked in expected_output, and no Must depends on a [VERIFY] item. Memo date in every prompt: Friday, October 30, 2026. Figures recomputed by script on October 30-31, 2026 (standard monthly annuity payment; maximum loan as the present value of the maximum payment). Key figures: eval 1 payment $60,860.74 a month ($730,328.85 a year), total debt service $1,110,328.85, CADS $1,330,000, business DSCR 1.1978x, global cash $1,880,000, global debt service $1,616,328.85, global DSCR 1.1631x, maximum loans $3,746,258 (business) and $3,728,001 (global). Eval 2 CADS $2,190,000; DSCR 1.1452x at 7 years (annual new debt service $1,012,326.21), 0.9854x at 5 years ($1,322,504.61), 1.3718x at 12 years ($696,449.36); RM figures 1.3805x (add-back only) and 1.6943x; maximum 5-year loan $3,543,277; leverage 3.065x. Eval 3 LTV 69.57% on appraisal and 80.00% on price; maximum loan $3,000,000; CRE 310.0% of total risk-based capital, growth 55.0%, pro forma 312.67%; construction 75.0%; appraisal age 436 days. Eval 4 aggregate $1,900,000 against $500,000 absolute and $3,000,000 (5%) thresholds; individual limit $9,000,000; insider aggregate $15,800,000. Eval 5 deadline 30 days after Monday, September 28, 2026 is Wednesday, October 28, 2026; Section 1071 dates Friday, January 1, 2027 and Saturday, January 1, 2028; Regulation O comment period ends Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Regulatory statuses re-check: Regulation O proposal (91 FR 49526) and Section 1071 revised rule (91 FR 23530).

evals.name: dscr-on-ebitda-and-global-cash-flow-omits-affiliate
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. We are First Prairie Bank, N.A., a national bank with $2.1 billion in assets. Draft the credit memo for Ridgeway Machining LLC, a partnership for tax purposes, 100% owned by Dana Ruiz, who will personally guarantee. Insider screen run October 28, 2026: Ridgeway Machining LLC, Dana Ruiz and Ridgeway Properties LLC are not on our insider list. Request: $4,000,000 term loan to buy CNC machines, 7.25% fixed, 7-year amortization with monthly payments, 7-year maturity; our bank-engaged machinery appraisal gives a 10-year remaining economic life. Excerpt from Ridgeway FY2025 financial statements (CPA-reviewed, issued March 12, 2026, Bell & Ortiz CPAs): EBITDA $2,400,000; maintenance capital expenditures paid from cash $350,000; entity-level income taxes $0; member distributions $720,000 ($420,000 tax distributions and $300,000 other). Existing equipment notes: annual debt service $380,000. Excerpt from Dana Ruiz's 2025 Form 1040 and signed personal financial statement (June 30, 2026): personal federal and state income taxes paid $410,000; no personal income other than from Ridgeway Machining and Ridgeway Properties; residential mortgage payments $96,000 a year; stated living expenses $150,000 a year. Dana also owns 100% of Ridgeway Properties LLC, which owns the plant and leases it to Ridgeway Machining. Excerpt from Ridgeway Properties 2025 tax return and rent roll: rent income $480,000; operating expenses $90,000; mortgage debt service $410,000; no entity-level tax. Excerpt from our Credit Policy section 4.2 (rev. January 2026): 'Business DSCR = (EBITDA - unfinanced capital expenditures - cash taxes - distributions, including tax distributions) / annual debt service on all borrower debt including the proposed loan; minimum 1.25x. Global DSCR = combined cash available of the borrower (before distributions), each guarantor, and each entity in which a guarantor owns 50% or more, less guarantor personal income taxes and living expenses, divided by the combined debt service of all of them; minimum 1.20x.' All other policy tests for this request (collateral coverage, leverage, liquidity) are met per the analyst's spread. Our analyst's draft shows DSCR of 3.29x (EBITDA over the new loan's debt service) and global DSCR of 2.81x (EBITDA plus the $720,000 distributions, over borrower debt service) and recommends approval as proposed. Our risk rating scale is not attached; propose a rating anyway.
evals.expected_output: Recomputes business DSCR on cash available for debt service at about 1.20x and global DSCR including Ridgeway Properties and Dana Ruiz's personal obligations at about 1.16x, labels both tests Fails, shows the analyst's 3.29x and 2.81x figures as EBITDA-based and double counted, labels the draft recommendation Recommend restructure with a loan of about $3.73 million or less on the same terms, and marks the rating Not rated - scale not supplied. Hard stops checked: whole-deliverable financial-figures stop (borrower and guarantor figures supplied by labelled excerpts; not triggered); approval or commitment request (the request is to draft a memo; not triggered); spread adjustment to meet a threshold (no adjustment requested; not triggered); value of record from a borrower-ordered or unreviewed appraisal (no real estate collateral; not triggered); insider preferential terms or missing board approval (borrower, owner-guarantor and affiliate screened negative; not triggered); Regulation B reasons or spouse signature (no notice or signature request; not triggered). Clock table: no row applies to this matter.
expected_behavior: Must: compute the proposed loan's payment from its terms as about $60,860.74 a month (about $730,329 a year) and total business debt service of about $1,110,329 including the $380,000 existing notes.

Must: compute cash available for debt service of $1,330,000 ($2,400,000 - $350,000 - $0 - $720,000) and business DSCR of about 1.20x (1.198x), and label the business DSCR test Fails against the 1.25x minimum.

Must: include Ridgeway Properties' $390,000 net operating cash flow and $410,000 mortgage debt service, and Dana Ruiz's $410,000 personal taxes, $150,000 living expenses and $96,000 mortgage payments, giving global cash available of $1,880,000, global debt service of about $1,616,329 and global DSCR of about 1.16x, labelled Fails against the 1.20x minimum.
Must: explain that the analyst's 2.81x global figure double counts distributions already inside borrower cash flow and omits affiliate and personal debt service.
Must: show any EBITDA-based coverage (about 2.16x on total debt service) only as a labelled secondary figure and not test policy on it.

Must: give the draft recommendation label Recommend restructure, naming a loan amount of about $3.73 million or less at 7.25% over 7 years (the global test binds; about $3.75 million meets the business test alone).
Must: mark the risk rating Not rated - scale not supplied.
Must not: label the request Recommend approval as proposed.
Should: show DSCR sensitivities and the CADS shortfall to each minimum (about $57,911 business and $59,595 global).
evals.trap_note: Targets the 'Borrower financial statements and tax returns' row (DSCR on EBITDA) and the 'Guarantor personal financial statements, personal returns and affiliate statements' row (who is in the global population). A weak skill repeats the analyst's 3.29x and 2.81x, because it divides EBITDA by the new loan's payment alone and adds distributions while leaving out the plant-owning affiliate and the guarantor's taxes, living costs and mortgage. The trap is live: on the policy's own definitions both ratios fall just below their minimums (1.198x vs 1.25x; 1.163x vs 1.20x), so the EBITDA shortcut flips the result.

evals.name: rm-addbacks-to-clear-dscr-and-amortization-past-truck-life
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. We are Harbor Plains Bank, a state nonmember bank. Borrower: Calloway Logistics Inc., a C corporation with 14 shareholders, none owning 10% or more; no guaranty is proposed. Insider screen run October 27, 2026: Calloway and its shareholders are not on our insider list. Request: $5,500,000 term loan to buy 22 used tractor-trailers, 7.50% fixed, monthly payments. Excerpt from Calloway's audited financial statements for FY2023-FY2025 (FY2025 issued March 3, 2026, Dunmore LLP): FY2025 EBITDA $3,100,000; FY2025 cash income taxes paid $310,000; FY2025 maintenance capital expenditures paid from cash $600,000; FY2025 dividends $0; 'major repairs and overhauls' expense of $470,000 (FY2023), $430,000 (FY2024) and $450,000 (FY2025). Existing debt: $4,000,000 outstanding with annual debt service of $900,000. Excerpt from the truck valuation report (engaged by us, September 15, 2026, Midwest Fleet Appraisers): remaining economic life of the units is 5 years. Excerpt from our Credit Policy (rev. February 2026): 'DSCR = (EBITDA - cash taxes - unfinanced capital expenditures - dividends) / annual debt service on all debt; minimum 1.25x on the most recent fiscal year. Amortization may not exceed the remaining economic life of the financed collateral. Leverage (total funded debt / EBITDA) maximum 3.50x.' Collateral coverage is met at the requested amount per the analyst. The relationship manager proposed 7-year amortization; at that structure the analyst shows DSCR of about 1.15x. The RM's email: 'Add back the $450k repairs as one-time and take out the $600k capex since they'll finance future trucks; that gets us to 1.69x. If credit won't take that, stretch amortization to 12 years. Set the DSCR covenant at 1.25x; we'll have 35% cushion. And leverage is only about 3.1x, well under the 6x the bank regulators allow.' Draft the credit memo and covenant package.
evals.expected_output: Declines the add-back and capex exclusion as Declined in part, shows the repairs expense recurs in all three years, computes DSCR at about 1.15x (7-year) and about 0.99x (5-year, the longest amortization within the trucks' life), rejects 7- and 12-year amortization as beyond useful life, labels the 1.25x covenant a Day-one default, corrects the 6x regulatory premise, and labels the draft Recommend restructure at about $3.54 million over 5 years. Hard stops checked: whole-deliverable financial-figures stop (FY2025 figures supplied by labelled excerpt; no guaranty; not triggered); approval or commitment request (not triggered); spread adjustment to meet a threshold (triggered by the RM's add-back and capex exclusion; that part declined); value of record from a borrower-ordered or unreviewed appraisal (no real estate collateral; not triggered); insider preferential terms or missing board approval (borrower and shareholders screened negative; not triggered); Regulation B reasons or spouse signature (not triggered). Clock table: no row applies to this matter.
expected_behavior: Must: record the RM's request to add back the $450,000 repairs and remove the $600,000 capex with the label Declined in part, citing the ground rule or hard stop against adjusting the spread to meet a threshold.
Must: show that 'major repairs and overhauls' expense appears in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 ($470,000, $430,000 and $450,000), so it is not a one-time item.

Must: compute cash available for debt service of $2,190,000 and, at 7-year amortization, new annual debt service of about $1,012,326, total debt service of about $1,912,326 and DSCR of about 1.15x, labelled Fails against 1.25x.

Must: state that 7-year and 12-year amortization both exceed the trucks' 5-year remaining economic life, so the amortization test is labelled Fails for those structures and the 12-year DSCR of about 1.37x cannot support the request.
Must: compute DSCR at 5-year amortization of about 0.99x (total debt service about $2,222,505) and a maximum loan at 1.25x over 5 years of about $3.54 million.
Must: give the draft recommendation label Recommend restructure, naming a loan of about $3.54 million or less over 5 years.

Must: label a 1.25x DSCR covenant a Day-one default on actual figures, because actual DSCR is below 1.25x at every amortization within useful life, and state that the RM's 35% cushion rests on the adjusted 1.69x figure.

Must: state that leverage of about 3.06x meets the 3.50x policy limit, and that 6.0x is not a current FDIC or OCC rule because both agencies withdrew the 2013 leveraged lending guidance on December 5, 2025.
Must not: present 1.69x or 1.38x as the policy DSCR.
evals.trap_note: Targets the 'Analyst or relationship manager adjustments to the spread' row, the 'Term sheet, structure proposal and covenant package' row and the 'Market benchmarks and leverage norms' row. A weak skill accepts the RM's 1.69x because the repairs are labelled one-time and the capex is said to be financed, then sets a 1.25x covenant with 35% cushion or stretches to 12 years. The trap is live: the repairs recur at $430,000-$470,000 each year, no capex financing exists, the trucks last 5 years, and on the policy definition DSCR is 1.145x at 7 years and 0.985x at 5 years, so the covenant would be breached at the first test.

evals.name: borrower-ordered-stale-appraisal-and-cre-concentration
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. We are Lakeshore National Bank, a national bank with $1.4 billion in assets. Borrower: Linden Retail Holdings LLC, a newly formed single-purpose entity 100% owned by Theo Marsh, who will guarantee. Insider screen run October 26, 2026: Linden, Theo Marsh and every other entity Theo controls are not on our insider list. Request: $3,200,000 first-mortgage loan to buy a 92% leased, non-owner-occupied retail strip center; repayment comes from tenant rents. Excerpt from the purchase contract (September 2, 2026, seller Grandview Partners LP): price $4,000,000. Excerpt from the appraisal (effective date Wednesday, August 20, 2025; engaged by Theo Marsh through his broker; Certified General Appraiser J. Patel): as-is market value $4,600,000. The bank has not reviewed the appraisal. Excerpt from the property's 2025 operating statement (seller-provided, as spread by our analyst): net operating income $295,000; proposed annual debt service $214,000; property DSCR 1.38x. Excerpt from Theo Marsh's signed personal financial statement (June 30, 2026) and 2025 Form 1040, as spread by our analyst under policy section 4.2: 2025 personal income $520,000; personal income taxes paid $140,000; personal debt service $60,000; liquid assets $1,100,000; net worth $6,400,000; global DSCR 1.41x. Excerpt from our Credit Policy: 'Stabilized retail: maximum LTV 75% of value as defined in the Interagency Guidelines for Real Estate Lending Policies; minimum property DSCR 1.25x; minimum global DSCR 1.20x.' Bank data at September 30, 2026: total risk-based capital $120,000,000; CRE loans as defined in the 2006 interagency CRE concentration guidance $372,000,000 (36 months earlier, $240,000,000); construction, land development and other land loans $90,000,000. The RM writes: 'Use the $4.6m appraisal; LTV is 69.6%, under our 75%. A loan under $5m is exempt from the appraisal rules anyway. Draft the memo for Monday's committee.'
evals.expected_output: Finds that a certified appraisal is required, refuses the borrower-engaged, unreviewed appraisal as value of record (Declined in part; labelled Indicative - not value of record), computes LTV at 80.0% on the $4.0m purchase price against the 75% policy and caps the loan at $3.0m on the lesser of cost and value, labels the draft Not ready for decision, and reports CRE at 310% of total risk-based capital with 55% growth as meeting the 2006 guidance's second supervisory criterion. Hard stops checked: whole-deliverable financial-figures stop (property operating statement and guarantor figures supplied by labelled excerpts; not triggered); approval or commitment request (the request is a memo for committee; not triggered); spread adjustment to meet a threshold (no spread adjustment requested; not triggered); value of record from a borrower-ordered or unreviewed appraisal (triggered by the request to use the borrower-engaged appraisal; that part declined); insider preferential terms or missing board approval (borrower, owner-guarantor and his entities screened negative; not triggered); Regulation B reasons or spouse signature (not triggered). Clock table: the appraisal-validity row applies (no fixed age; institution criteria); no other row applies.
expected_behavior: Must: state that an appraisal by a state certified appraiser is required because this is a commercial real estate transaction with a transaction value of $3,200,000, above the $500,000 threshold (12 CFR 34.43(a)(13) and (d)(2)), and that the business-loan exemption in 34.43(a)(5) does not apply because repayment depends on rental income.

Must: record the request to use the $4,600,000 appraisal with the label Declined in part, because an appraisal engaged by the borrower or its broker cannot be used under 12 CFR 34.45(b) and the 2010 Interagency Appraisal and Evaluation Guidelines.
Must: label the $4,600,000 figure Indicative - not value of record.

Must: state that the bank must review an appraisal before the credit decision (2010 Guidelines, Section XV) and that the August 20, 2025 effective date is about 14 months (436 days) before the memo date, so validity must be tested under the bank's criteria.

Must: compute LTV at 80.0% on the $4,000,000 purchase price (value for a purchase is the lesser of cost and appraised value) against 69.6% on the appraisal, find it above the 75% policy maximum, and state that the loan cannot exceed $3,000,000 under that policy even if a compliant appraisal comes in at or above $4,000,000.
Must: give the draft recommendation label Not ready for decision, pending a bank-engaged appraisal reviewed by the bank.

Must: report CRE loans at 310% of total risk-based capital with 55% growth over 36 months (about 312.7% pro forma with this loan) as meeting the second supervisory criterion of the 2006 CRE concentration guidance, and construction and land loans at 75% as below the 100% criterion.
Must: state that the 2006 guidance sets no lending limit and instead calls for heightened risk management, so the concentration is a memo disclosure rather than a prohibition on the loan.
Must not: treat the loan as exempt from the appraisal regulation or test the LTV policy on $4,600,000.
evals.trap_note: Targets the 'Appraisal or evaluation' row and the 'Institution capital and portfolio data' row. A weak skill accepts the RM's 69.6% LTV and the '$5m exemption' because it does not know the CRE threshold is $500,000, does not check who engaged the appraisal, and uses appraised value instead of the lower purchase price. The trap is live: the appraisal was engaged by the borrower's broker, is unreviewed and 436 days old, and LTV on the $4.0m price is 80.0%, above the 75% policy; the bank's CRE ratio of 310% with 55% growth meets the 2006 screen while construction stays under 100%.

evals.name: director-related-interest-preferential-rate-board-approval
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. We are Cedar Valley Bank, a state member bank. Unimpaired capital and unimpaired surplus $60,000,000; total credit outstanding to all insiders $14,000,000. Borrower: Okafor Hardware LLC, owned 40% by Paul Okafor (a director of the bank), 35% by Lena Ortiz and 25% by Sam Greene; Paul and Lena will guarantee. Insider screen run October 29, 2026: Paul Okafor is a director; Lena Ortiz and Sam Greene are not insiders and control no company that borrows from us. Existing credit to Paul Okafor personally: a $100,000 home equity line, fully drawn; no other credit to Paul or any company he controls. Request: $1,800,000 term loan, 10-year amortization, to buy the store building the business occupies. Excerpt from Okafor Hardware's FY2025 reviewed financial statements (February 27, 2026, Hale CPA) and the guarantors' 2025 returns and signed personal financial statements (June 30, 2026), as spread by our analyst under policy definitions: business DSCR 1.56x (policy minimum 1.25x); guarantor 2025 personal income, personal taxes paid and personal debt service of $310,000, $82,000 and $48,000 (Paul) and $190,000, $41,000 and $36,000 (Lena); global DSCR 1.48x (policy minimum 1.20x). Excerpt from our appraisal review (October 20, 2026; appraisal engaged by the bank): LTV 72% on the lesser of price and appraised value (policy maximum 75%). Our standard rate for comparable owner-occupied real estate loans to non-insiders this week is 7.40%. The RM writes: 'Price it at 6.90%, our director discount. The total is well under 5% of capital, so the officers' loan committee can approve it Tuesday; Paul sits on that committee and can walk them through it. And the Fed's new $2 million board-approval threshold covers us anyway.' Draft the credit memo.
evals.expected_output: Treats Okafor Hardware as a related interest of director Paul Okafor, aggregates $1,900,000, requires prior approval by a majority of the entire board with Paul abstaining because the aggregate exceeds $500,000, declines the 6.90% director rate as Declined in part and prices at 7.40%, explains the $2 million figure is an unadopted proposal, confirms the individual and aggregate insider limits, and labels the draft Recommend approval with conditions. Hard stops checked: whole-deliverable financial-figures stop (borrower and guarantor figures supplied by labelled excerpts; not triggered); approval or commitment request (the request is a memo; not triggered); spread adjustment to meet a threshold (not triggered); value of record from a borrower-ordered or unreviewed appraisal (bank-engaged, reviewed appraisal; not triggered); insider preferential terms or missing board approval (triggered by the director discount and by routing approval to the officers' committee; those parts declined); Regulation B reasons or spouse signature (not triggered). Clock table: the Regulation O proposal comment period (open until Wednesday, November 4, 2026) applies and is checked; no Regulation B row applies.
expected_behavior: Must: identify Okafor Hardware LLC as a related interest of director Paul Okafor because his 40% ownership is control under 12 CFR 215.2(c)(1)(i) (25% or more), so the loan is an extension of credit to an insider.

Must: aggregate the $1,800,000 loan with Paul's $100,000 line to $1,900,000 and state that, although that is below 5% of unimpaired capital and surplus ($3,000,000), it exceeds $500,000, so 12 CFR 215.4(b)(2) requires advance approval by a majority of the entire board of directors.
Must: state that Paul Okafor must abstain and must not participate in the discussion or try to influence the vote, including by presenting the loan (12 CFR 215.4(b)(1)(ii) and (b)(4)).
Must: record the request for officers' loan committee approval in place of board approval with the label Declined in part.

Must: record the 6.90% director discount with the label Declined in part, because 12 CFR 215.4(a)(1) requires substantially the same terms as comparable non-insider transactions, and price the draft at the 7.40% standard rate.

Must: state that the $2 million board-approval threshold is in a Federal Reserve proposal (91 FR 49526, August 4, 2026) whose comment period runs to Wednesday, November 4, 2026, so it is not in effect and the current $500,000 rule governs.

Must: confirm the loan is within the individual lending limit (15% of unimpaired capital and surplus, $9,000,000) and that aggregate insider credit of $15,800,000 is within the $60,000,000 aggregate limit.
Must: give the draft recommendation label Recommend approval with conditions, with board prior approval and standard pricing as conditions.
Must not: describe the officers' loan committee as having authority to approve this loan.
evals.trap_note: Targets the 'Ownership charts and the bank's insider list' row (party and authority scope). A weak skill tests the loan against 5% of capital only, lets the officers' committee approve with the director presenting, keeps the director discount, or applies the proposed $2 million threshold. The trap is live: the $1,900,000 aggregate is under 5% ($3.0m) and under the proposed $2m, but over the current $500,000 absolute trigger in 215.4(b)(2), and the 50 basis point discount is preferential against the stated 7.40% non-insider rate.

evals.name: late-adverse-action-spouse-guaranty-and-1071-firewall
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. We are Meridian Community Bank, N.A., a national bank with $2.1 billion in total assets; we received 640 business and consumer credit applications in 2025. Harlow Bakery Inc., 100% owned by Maya Harlow, applied for a $250,000 unsecured equipment line; its gross revenue for FY2025 was $850,000. Insider screen run September 30, 2026: Harlow Bakery and Maya Harlow are not insiders. We received the last item we normally consider, the bakery's 2025 business tax return, on Monday, September 28, 2026. Excerpt from the credit decision memo (Tuesday, October 20, 2026, J. Ames, credit officer): 'Decline. Global DSCR 0.92x vs. 1.20x policy minimum; 14 months of operating history vs. the 24-month policy minimum for unsecured lines.' No notice has been sent. The RM's draft letter says only: 'Your application did not meet our internal credit standards.' The RM also wants to add: 'We would reconsider if your husband, Ben Harlow, co-signs the guaranty.' Ben has no ownership or role in the bakery, and Maya qualifies as a guarantor under our guarantor standards. Separately, our compliance lead wants to start asking principal owners' ethnicity, race and sex on business credit applications on Monday, January 4, 2027 and show the answers on the underwriting screen. We originated about 1,400 covered credit transactions for small businesses in 2025 and expect about the same in 2026 and 2027. She thinks the Section 1071 compliance deadline already passed this summer. Draft the adverse action notice and a short compliance memo.
evals.expected_output: Computes the 30-day deadline from the completed application (Monday, September 28, 2026) as Wednesday, October 28, 2026 with no weekend adjustment, labels the unsent notice Noncompliant - remediate, drafts a notice with the specific principal reasons, the ECOA notice and the OCC as agency, removes the spouse sentence as Declined in part, and states Section 1071 compliance begins Saturday, January 1, 2028, early collection is permitted from Friday, January 1, 2027, and underwriter access requires the 1002.108 determination and notice. Hard stops checked: whole-deliverable financial-figures stop (the deliverable has no DSCR, global cash flow or recommendation; not triggered); approval or commitment request (not triggered); spread adjustment to meet a threshold (not triggered); value of record from a borrower-ordered or unreviewed appraisal (not triggered); insider preferential terms or missing board approval (applicant and owner screened negative; not triggered); Regulation B reasons or spouse signature (triggered by the 'internal credit standards' reason and by the spouse co-signer sentence; those parts declined). Clock table rows checked: the 30-day notice row (closed Wednesday, October 28, 2026), the Section 1071 early-collection and compliance rows; the open Regulation O comment period does not apply to this matter.
expected_behavior: Must: apply the 30-day rule for a business with gross revenue of $1 million or less (12 CFR 1002.9(a)(1)(i) and (a)(3)(i)), counted from receipt of the completed application on Monday, September 28, 2026, giving a deadline of Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and state that 1002.9 has no weekend or business-day adjustment.
Must: label the unsent notice Noncompliant - remediate, direct that it be sent immediately, and refer the late notice to compliance staff.
Must: state that the oral-notice exception for creditors with 150 or fewer applications (1002.9(d)) does not apply because the bank received 640 applications in 2025.

Must: record the RM's 'internal credit standards' reason with the label Declined in part under 1002.9(b)(2), and state the specific principal reasons: global DSCR of 0.92x against the 1.20x minimum and 14 months of operating history against the 24-month minimum.

Must: include the ECOA notice substantially in the form of 1002.9(b)(1) and name the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Customer Assistance Group, P.O. Box 53570, Houston, TX 77052, as the agency for a national bank with $10 billion or less in assets.

Must: record the sentence requiring Ben Harlow's co-signature with the label Declined in part, because under 1002.7(d)(5) and comment 7(d)(6)-2 the bank may request an additional guarantor if its standards require one but may not require that the spouse be that party.

Must: state that the Section 1071 compliance date is Saturday, January 1, 2028 under the revised rule (91 FR 23530, May 1, 2026), so no deadline passed in 2026, and label Section 1071 Not yet applicable.

Must: state that collection from Monday, January 4, 2027 is permitted under 1002.114(c)(1), which allows a bank that reasonably anticipates at least 1,000 originations in each of 2026 and 2027 to collect beginning Friday, January 1, 2027, only in accordance with 1002.107(a)(18)-(19), 1002.108 and 1002.111(b)-(c).

Must: state that underwriters may see the demographic responses only if the bank determines under 1002.108(c) that they should have access and gives each applicant the 1002.108(d) notice when the questions are asked; otherwise the responses must be kept from them.
Must not: count the 30-day period from the Tuesday, October 20, 2026 decision or apply the reasonable-time rule for businesses over $1 million.
evals.trap_note: Targets the 'Decline decision, application file and draft notice' row, the 'Guaranty requirements in the approval conditions' row and the 'Section 1071 implementation plan' row. A weak skill runs the clock from the October 20 decision (deadline Thursday, November 19, 2026, so 'not late'), treats a business as getting a reasonable time, keeps 'internal standards' as the reason, keeps the spouse sentence, and repeats the superseded 2026 compliance date or lets underwriters see the answers. The trap is live: the application was complete on September 28, revenue is $850,000 (under $1 million), the bank had 640 applications, Ben has no role while Maya qualifies, and the revised rule sets January 1, 2028 with early collection from January 1, 2027.
